subStrands.name: Functions, Sections, Departments, Personnel and Layout

objectives.description: Definition of an office; functions — receiving information, recording information, processing/analysing information, giving information, storing information, safeguarding/protecting assets.
Sections of an office: reception, general office, stores, mail room/registry.
Departments: accounts, purchasing, sales, personnel/human resource, production, legal, administration, transport.

Office personnel: office manager, office supervisor, general clerks, accounts clerks, data entry clerks, administrative assistants, secretaries (company secretary, private secretary, stenographer secretary), receptionist, typist, messenger.
Professional image of office staff: personal and business attributes; social habits, personal hygiene and healthy lifestyle; time management — time management skills and time wasters in the office.
Office layout: open and closed office layout — factors that determine choice of office layout; advantages and disadvantages of open and closed layout.

Principles of organisation: unity of objectives, span of control, authority and responsibility, delegation, unity of functions, unity of command, supervision, remuneration, accountability, esprit de corps.
Organisational structure: line structure, line and staff structure, staff structure, functional structure, matrix structure; organisational chart/organogram — uses, advantages and disadvantages.

Documents used in business transactions: letter of enquiry, price list/catalogue/quotation, local purchase order, order, proforma invoice, invoice, delivery note/waybill, debit note, credit note, statement of account, cheques/payment orders, receipt, purchase requisition — identify, complete and use each document.
Methods of payment: cash, cheque, standing order, credit transfer, money transfer — advantages and disadvantages of each.

Payroll handling: terminologies — wages, salaries, gross pay, net pay, allowances, basic pay and PAYE; methods of determining workers' pay — piece rate, time rate, commission, flat rate, overtime and bonus; preparation of payroll.
Tax regimes: VAT, income tax, communication service tax (CST), property tax, import/customs duty.
Petty cash: petty cash and imprest system; completion of the petty cash book.

subStrands.name: Banking, Types of Accounts, Cheques and Stock Control

objectives.description: Types of bank: commercial, development, merchant, rural/community banks and the central bank; types of bank accounts — savings, current, fixed deposit; definition, types, features of a valid cheque, parties to a cheque and reasons for dishonouring cheques; crossed cheques, various ways of crossing a cheque and the effect of the crossing.

Stock procedure: ordering of stock; duties of the storekeeper; requisition procedure; stock record and stocktaking (annual, periodic, perpetual); stock control (minimum stock, maximum stock, re-order level); stock valuation (cost price, average price, market price, lower price).

subStrands.name: Office Machines, ICT, Communication and Filing Systems

objectives.description: General office machines/equipment: computer, photocopier, risograph, collating machine, dictaphone, typewriters, duplicating machines, perforator, calculator, cash register, pager, fax machines, accounting machines, scanner — factors for purchasing, uses, advantages and disadvantages, maintenance.

The computer and ICT: meaning, components, types, peripheral devices, functions, uses, advantages and disadvantages of computers; basic terms used in computing; functions of the internet, intranet and the world wide web; service providers.
Mail room equipment/materials: letter opening machine, addressing machine, franking machine, shredding machine, scales, scissors/paper knife/blade, stapling machine, staple remover, guillotine.

Communication: meaning, forms (verbal — oral and written; non-verbal; visual); channels of communication; barriers to effective communication (organisational, physical, psychological, socio-cultural barriers).

Business correspondence: letters (form letters, circulars), memos, reports (short formal, short informal, periodic/routine, special, statutory) — parts, formats and uses; mail handling — procedures for incoming and outgoing mail.

Meetings: purpose and kinds of meetings; requirements for a valid meeting; duties of officials — chairperson, secretary, teller, scrutineer; meeting terminologies (notice, quorum, agenda, resolution, ad-hoc committee, minutes, motion, ex-officio, casting vote etc.); preparation of meeting documents — notice, agenda, minutes.

Filing and indexing: methods of classification — alphabetical, numerical, subject, geographical, chronological, alpha-numeric, subject-numeric; systems of filing — lateral, suspension, vertical, horizontal; rules for filing; indexing and cross-referencing; electronic filing; central and departmental filing.

strands.name: Reference Books, Post Office and Human Relations

subStrands.name: Reference Sources, Postal Services, Human Relations, Health and Employment

objectives.description: Reference books and sources of information: general reference books (dictionary, encyclopaedia, almanac), places (atlas, site plan), specialised reference books (trade journals, post office guide, telephone directory), government publications (Hansard, white paper, gazette, financial instructions, general orders); business information (exchange rates, stock exchange listing, financial bulletins, employment opportunities).

Post office services: postal services (postage stamps, express mail, special mail, poste restante, private mail bag, registered mail, recorded delivery, airmail, business reply service, private mail box); courier services (EMS, DHL, FedEx); agency services; remittance services (postal order, money transfer).
Human relations: internal relations in the office; relations with the public; interpersonal skills — factors that promote public relations and ways of improving interpersonal skills.

Health, safety and welfare in the office: health hazards in the office — types and prevention; accidents in the office — types, causes and measures to prevent; staff welfare — welfare services and benefits.
Pre-employment procedures: advertisement; submission of letters of application and curriculum vitae; the interview.

Entrepreneurship and small-scale business: meaning of entrepreneur and general characteristics of an entrepreneur; small scale business — characteristics of a small scale enterprise; importance of small scale businesses in the society.

subStrands.name: Proofreading, Spelling, Word Division and Punctuation

objectives.description: Proofreading and office abbreviations: importance and purpose of proofreading; correction of errors in passages; expansion of office abbreviations and use them correctly.
Spelling, word division and punctuation: basic rules for spellings, word division and punctuation.
